interpretations.text: Within the finite-budget native MuJoCo sequence search, the best found signed maximum excess J was 11.816439876751495, down by 8.61034587631497 from the baseline value 20.426785753066465. The holding-speed metric decreased from 0.4285357150613293 m/s to 0.2536984073471587 m/s, but holding maximum position error increased from 0.12402622706010982 m to 0.12816439876751495 m. Thus, the lower aggregate worst-constraint score does not mean every diagnostic metric improved. The limiting sampled constraint also changed: the baseline was limited by holding speed, whereas the best candidate was limited by holding position at 0.45 s. Its 0.12816439876751495 m error exceeded the 0.01 m limit, producing the positive normalized excess 11.816439876751495. Therefore, the best candidate remained a valid evaluated task failure under the sampled diagnostic constraints.

The search stopped because its evaluation-request budget was exhausted after 120 optimization evaluations, 120 rollouts, and 120,000 native physics steps; convergence and global optimality were not established. Consequently, failure to find a passing sequence does not establish global nonlinear infeasibility, structural infeasibility, or a solver-independent capability limit. Task acceptance itself remains unmeasured, and the evidence does not establish continuous-time compliance, hardware performance, robustness, repeatability, or equilibrium validity. It also cannot distinguish among control parameterization, finite search budget, local-search limitations, and true model-level capability limits as explanations for the remaining violation.

The missing discriminating evidence is an applicable full 0-to-0.5 s replay from the frozen initial state with independent frozen task-acceptance checks, including all holding-window requirements rather than only the declared sampled proxies. Additional evidence would also be required to determine whether the residual failure persists beyond this particular 24-dimensional bounded search and finite evaluation budget. Until those checks exist, the recorded control schedule is only a finite-budget native-model candidate, not an observed task pass or proof of infeasibility.

The registered physical execution was a valid but failed task evaluation. Terminal position error was 0.1264496051238062 m against a 0.01 m limit, an excess of 0.1164496051238062 m. Holding maximum position error was 0.12816439876751495 m against 0.01 m, exceeding the limit by 0.11816439876751495 m; this was the dominant normalized constraint violation (11.816439876751495). Holding maximum speed was 0.2536984073471587 m/s against 0.02 m/s, an excess of 0.2336984073471587 m/s. Force-bound violation was exactly 0.0 N and passed its 1e-08 N limit, while solver-error count was exactly 0 and passed its zero-error requirement. Thus the observed failure concerns position and motion acceptance, not recorded force-bound or solver-error violations.

The late trajectory observations support the descriptive explanation that the system had not settled during the holding assessment. At 0.45 s, speed was 0.2536984073471587 m/s with tip velocity [0.0822753779226852, -0.10703684124359165, 0.21479468963351572] m/s. At 0.50 s, speed remained 0.18958003507412524 m/s with velocity [-0.05632481680159382, -0.00602278801184894, -0.1809194039774003] m/s, including reversals in the first and third components. This is consistent with continued motion and the failed 0.02 m/s holding-speed requirement. However, these observations do not identify a mechanical or control cause: no diagnostic relations or recorded control diagnostics are available, and position error is unavailable in both cited samples. The evidence therefore cannot distinguish oscillation, insufficient damping, inadequate control authority, poor targeting, or another mechanism.

Feasibility, robustness, repeatability, hardware performance, and continuous-time compliance remain unresolved. A single physical launch establishes only this observed task outcome; it does not demonstrate global nonlinear or structural infeasibility. The configured termination conditions include duration and numerical failure, but they are not an observed termination reason, and the zero solver-error count does not support attributing this failure to a solver fault. Discriminating evidence would require additional registered executions or trajectory/control diagnostics linking commands, tensions, position error, and motion over the holding interval; none are available here.

The capability analysis did not complete: computation status is execution_incomplete, verification is insufficient, and the mathematical conclusion is inconclusive. No solver result, verified witness, exclusion certificate, task-acceptance decision, or reported task metric is available. The declared model has 48 generalized coordinates and six tendon-tension inputs bounded from 0 to 8 N, applied pre-step in tendon order at a 0.01 s control period. The analysis window was 0–0.5 s and covered the required sample times, but the terminal-error, holding-error, and holding-speed constraints were evaluated only as diagnostic sampled proxies rather than by a full acceptance replay. Resource use was at least 371 physics steps, one charged analysis, and 1.2827493000077084 s of both charged numerical time and worker-wall elapsed time; these costs do not establish computational efficiency because there is no comparison or preference criterion.

Task feasibility remains unresolved. Execution failure cannot be interpreted as infeasibility, while constraint expressibility and sample coverage do not demonstrate feasibility. In particular, the evidence cannot support task acceptance, whole holding-window or continuous-time compliance, global nonlinear feasibility or infeasibility, structural infeasibility, equilibrium validity, hardware performance, robustness, or repeatability. No failure mechanism can be supported or weakened because there are no critical observations, diagnostic relations, solver diagnostics, constraint values, or trajectory metrics. The evidence also does not identify whether incompleteness arose from the solver, the operating point, implementation, or the tested design hypothesis.

Discrimination requires evidence from a completed numerical evaluation: solver status and diagnostics, a fully replayed native trajectory from the standardized initial state, and numerical values for every terminal and holding-window constraint sample. A verified feasible witness would support capability within the declared MuJoCo model and sampled scope; a valid exclusion certificate would support only the corresponding certified infeasibility scope. Without either, no physical or global conclusion is justified.

original_plan.expected_observation: At least one legal changed structure, after its own full-horizon bounded control optimization, lowers holding maximum position error below 0.12816439876751495 m and holding maximum speed below 0.2536984073471587 m/s without worsening terminal error beyond 0.1264496051238062 m or introducing force-bound or solver violations; a successful candidate meets 0.01 m terminal error, 0.01 m holding error, and 0.02 m/s holding speed together.
original_plan.fixed_conditions: Keep the frozen task identity, target [0.29, -0.035, 0.19] m, 0.5 s horizon, 0.01 s control period and sample period, 0.0005 s timestep, final 0.05 s holding window, all physical input bounds, model/source/fidelity contracts, and independent full-task evaluation unchanged. Do not reuse an old control schedule as evidence for a changed structure; optimize control for each structure.
original_plan.hypothesis: The current failure is not established as structural infeasibility; a legal mixed search over authorized geometry, routing, and segment variables, with control reoptimized for every proposed structure, can materially reduce the dominant late holding-position violation and residual speed while preserving force and solver validity, potentially satisfying all frozen Reach/Hold constraints.
original_plan.interpretation: The saved native optimization improved aggregate excess but worsened holding position, and the independent replay showed continued late motion with valid bounds and no solver errors. This supports testing coupled structural authority/settling changes rather than merely replaying the same failed schedule. Improvements and degradations will be compared at matched evidence scope.
original_plan.stopping_condition: Stop this hypothesis test when a legal candidate passes all frozen constraints in independent full-task physical evaluation, or when the admitted mixed-search budget/window is exhausted with sealed execution records; finite failure will be reported only as bounded search failure, not infeasibility.
original_plan.weakening_observation: Across a fair legal mixed search with per-structure control adaptation, independently comparable candidates fail to improve the dominant holding-position error or systematically trade it against terminal error and speed, while force and numerical validity remain intact.

original_plan.expected_observation: At least one legal changed structure with its own full-task Native control optimization improves holding maximum position error below 0.12816439876751495 m and holding maximum speed below 0.2536984073471587 m/s while preserving force bounds, solver validity, complete execution, and without materially worsening terminal error from 0.1264496051238062 m; a passing proposal would satisfy all frozen thresholds.

original_plan.interpretation: A full-task pass would support the mixed structure-control hypothesis and trigger acceptance-certificate reading before formal SELECT. original_plan.stopping_condition: Stop this search after at most 12 legal structure proposals and 12 complete condition evaluations, using at most 180 Native rollout callbacks per condition and 12 control-search iterations, or earlier if a proposal obtains an independently evaluated full-task pass or execution records seal at the interface boundary.
original_plan.weakening_observation: Across the evaluated legal proposals, fresh per-structure control optimization yields no independently comparable improvement in the dominant holding-position error, or improvements systematically trade against terminal error or holding speed while remaining far above frozen limits. This weakens the proposed direction but does not prove structural infeasibility because the search is finite.

claimed_inference.description: Use empirical_search for a proposed experiment, including testing a prediction in physics. Unsupported stronger claims remain annotated hypotheses and do not veto an otherwise legal experiment. Formal conclusions and SELECT/CONFIRM/STOP still require registered scoped evidence; execution always requires valid identity, authorization, applicability and budget.

selected_candidate.description: Required for execute/initialize_control/control_search/physical_replay. Match candidate, control_seed.candidate, control_search.candidate or physical_replay.candidate respectively; never substitute the control source. For diagnose, place the owned candidate here at decision.selected_candidate; there is no top-level selected_candidate field.

ScientificControlEffort.description: Scientific effort, compiled to the existing LocalControlSearchSettings.

evaluation_requests.description: Maximum Native rollout callbacks per condition; separate from iterations and formal mathematical evaluation charges.

iterations.description: Independent iteration cap. If omitted: min(callback cap, frozen Study iteration cap, original contract maximum). Early convergence can use fewer callbacks/iterations.

knot_count.description: Uniform knots over the chosen adjustment window. Evaluation always covers the complete frozen task. Local windows require at least one interior knot; endpoint corrections remain zero.

control_treatment.description: reoptimized: fresh Native control optimization. not_optimized: static/held-input proxy. proxy_optimized: the registered CONIC task_violation optimizes affine-model controls, not Native dynamics.

design_variable_groups.description: Real structure groups only. Control reoptimization is specified separately by control_treatment.

initial_tension_n.description: Native common absolute initial tension. Omit only to use the unique frozen tendon pretension default; if unavailable an explicit choice is required.

proxy_objective.description: Required for mathematical_proxy; never substituted for Native task capability.

section_types.description: Omit to retain original prototype section kinds; dimension changes still use frozen domains.

segment_counts.description: Omit for frozen singleton topology. Explicit out-of-domain choices are rejected, never clamped.

function.description: Search curated procedural guidance, then execute a result entry read_query exactly. A retrieval receipt artifact ID is not an entry_id. Historical guidance never grants scientific evidence or action permission.
